To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the digital chest drainage system (DCDS) reduces the duration of chest drainage, the length of hospitalization, and the inter-observer variability.

the use of a novel digital drainage system compared with a standard drainage system reduces the inter-observer variability in assessing the presence of air leaks, and that the use of this novel system may help in differentiating between an active air leak and a pleural space efflux.
digital chest drain systems may reduce the length of hospitalization after pulmonary resection and that digital systems may be useful for predicting patients at high risk of prolonged air leaks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a prospective randomized trial comparing an electronic chest drainage with a traditional one.
the development and application of a digital chest drainage system in patients undergoing pulmonary resection.
the development of an intelligent, portable and wearable chest drainage system that can be used in the operating room and in the postoperative ward.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the digital chest drain system is a useful and feasible tool to monitor the patient in the postoperative period, allowing a better assessment of air leaks, and reducing the length of hospitalization and the duration of chest drainage.
this trial will provide new evidence about the use of a new digital chest drain system compared with a conventional chest drain system in the management of air leaks following pulmonary lobectomy.

this trial is a randomized, multicenter, prospective trial that will evaluate the clinical impact and the feasibility of digital drainage systems in patients undergoing pulmonary lobectomies for benign and malignant disease through a standard three port video-assisted thoracoscopic approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic drainage system (DreTec™ Palm Evo) is feasible and safe, and it may help in reducing the length of postoperative hospital stay.

we have demonstrated a reduction of hospital stay and a reduction in the duration of chest drainage in patients who have been randomized to the digital drainage system compared with the traditional one.

this study is designed to compare an innovative digital chest drainage system (the Drentech™ Palm) with the traditional chest drainage system in patients undergoing pulmonary resection for both benign and malignancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digital chest drain systems are feasible and safe and may be used in patients submitted to major lung resection.
the use of a new electronic system may reduce the inter-observer variability and the time for chest tube removal.
digital drainage systems may be a valuable tool for the management of air leaks.
